text:
The Senators have points in seven straight (5-0-2), and they earned it, with 59% of the expected goals in that run (expected goals measure the quality of chances). The man at the back of it is Linus Ullmark. Last season he finished 13.3 goals worse than an average goalie would have on the same shots. This season he is 10.3 better, with a .940 save rate. That's not a hot week, that's a different goalie.

Ottawa has also had a strange, emotional fortnight. Nick Cousins was hurt by a heavy hit from Jakob Chychrun earlier this month and has since come back into a bigger role, up to 12:12 a night with William Eklund out until January. Tyler Boucher scored the winner in his NHL debut in Winnipeg, with his father Brian, the former NHL goalie, watching. Thursday they blew a three-goal lead and lost 6-5 to the Flyers in overtime, so there is a sour taste to wash out.

The Kings are the opposite case: better than their record. They are minus 11 in goal difference despite plus 2.5 in expected goals, because their finishing (6.9 goals short of what their chances usually produce) and their goaltending (Darcy Kuemper at 5.2 goals below expected) keep giving it back. Thursday's shootout win in Toronto, after trailing by three, is the kind of night that suggests the bounces are owed. Kevin Fiala, back nine months after his frightening Olympic injury, sits one assist from 300, and Artemi Panarin is off the out list and day-to-day. Drew Doughty, heading toward free agency, has hired Pat Brisson as his agent.

These two met on Oct 29 and the Kings won 6-5 in overtime, a game they deserved 86% of the time. Our playoff race gives Ottawa an 89% chance and Los Angeles 33%, which is why a team this good on paper can't afford many more nights like the first month.
headline: Ullmark's revival meets the Kings' bad math
